summary: FortiGate FG-EDGE-01 denied 14 outbound UDP/161 (SNMP) connection attempts from internal host 192.0.2.10 to 192.0.2.20 under policy 784 (TEMP-DENY-LOG). Each logged session recorded zero duration, zero bytes and zero packets.
assessment: The firewall blocked every logged attempt, and the zero byte and packet counters confirm no session was established and no data was exchanged. The repetition of the same source, destination and service is consistent with two competing explanations that the supplied evidence cannot separate: a misconfigured or newly deployed monitoring agent retrying SNMP polling against a host that no longer permits it, or internal enumeration of SNMP services. The policy name TEMP-DENY-LOG suggests a temporary rule, which raises the likelihood of a legitimate service being caught by a recent policy change. Overall risk is assessed as low because the traffic was denied and no compromise is demonstrated; the verdict is suspicious rather than benign because the originating process and business purpose have not been established. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate reconnaissance, exploitation, malware, command and control, or compromise.
recommended_actions: Identify the asset and owner of 192.0.2.10 and confirm whether an SNMP monitoring agent is installed and expected to poll 192.0.2.20.
Review endpoint telemetry on 192.0.2.10 to determine which process initiated the UDP/161 traffic.
Confirm when policy 784 (TEMP-DENY-LOG) was created and whether it was intended to block this traffic.
Correlate historical firewall logs for the same source and service to establish whether this pattern predates the policy change.
missing_information: Asset owner and business role of 192.0.2.10
Process that initiated the SNMP traffic
Change record or intent behind policy 784
Historical baseline for SNMP traffic between these hosts
Whether the same source attempted other services or destinations in the same window
